subject: SOC2 reattestation — evidence archival window & burst capacity path
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Lena Ortiz <l.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: SOC2 re-attest + retention window question for renewal

Hi Lauren,

We're kicking off our renewal discussions and security is asking for clarification on Redwood's SOC 2 re-attestation plan. Two asks from our side: (1) can you confirm whether Redwood will provide an updated SOC 2 attestation ahead of our Nov 17 renewal date, and (2) we need to expand the log retention window to 13 months (up from our current 12) for audit consistency.

Also, legal flagged a potential need for a short-term burst/capacity uplift during the evidence handoff window (roughly 48–72 hours) to run exports and backing snapshots. Could you outline the evidence delivery approach (sample logs, timeline, and the mechanics for an expanded retention window)? Any rough cadence and impacts to pricing would be helpful so we can align procurement.

Thanks — Jared
Jared Mills
Director, IS & Compliance
Acme Health
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attest + retention window question for renewal

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear asks. We're aligned to support a SOC 2 re-attestation ahead of your renewal. High level next steps I propose: 

- I'll attach our SOC2-Checklist-2026.xlsx (first pass) that outlines the evidence categories and typical deliverables.
- Schedule a 30-min technical sync on Oct 14 to walk through the export mechanics and retention implications.
- Engineering will propose a short-term burst capacity path for the 48–72h staging/export window and we will surface a price delta for the amendment.

Marcus, can you confirm what sample exports we can produce and whether a 13-month retention is feasible as a contract amendment? Priya — I expect you'll draft the amendment language once we agree terms.

I'll hold a tentative slot on Oct 14 at 11:00 PT; happy to move.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attest + retention window question for renewal

Hi team — quick technical note before the sync.

- Evidence we can provide: structured audit logs (auth, admin actions, model route logs), config snapshots, and a redacted sample of per-request metadata. I've attached a small sample bundle for reference (logs-sample-2026.tar.gz).
- Retention: extending to 13 months is straightforward on the storage side; we will schedule a policy change that reindexes objects and update retention metadata. It will require a one-time storage reclassification job (non-disruptive).
- Burst capacity: for the 48–72h export window we can provision a dedicated node pool or enable a temporary throughput burst on your Dedicated pool. Rough sizing: to support an export throughput of ~10k tokens/minute sustained during the window, we recommend a short-term reserved burst. That approach minimizes impact on your baseline production traffic.

Estimate on cost: ballpark +~18% on current committed rate for the window and data egress/export labor. I'll put a formal quote together but want to confirm the target throughput and exact export artifacts first.

On the Oct 14 sync I'll bring the ops plan and a checklist for evidence handoff.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Lena Ortiz <l.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attest + retention window question for renewal

Thanks Lauren and Marcus — that all sounds reasonable.

Two clarifications: (1) Acme requests retention to be 13 months in the contract amendment (not a product-side workaround), and (2) procurement wants the capacity uplift scoped as a line item (10k tpm for 72 hours) so it can be budgeted separately.

Can Priya or legal propose amendment language and a DocuSign link we can circulate? We'd like to aim for signed amendments by Oct 22 so we can run the evidence export the week of Oct 26 and have attestation artifacts in time for renewal documentation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Jared
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acmehealth.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 re-attest + retention window question for renewal

Hi Jared,

Thanks — attaching a capacity quote and a draft amendment for the 13-month retention carve-out (capacity-quote-2026.pdf). Key points: 

- Amendment: retention extension to 13 months (remains customer-managed retention, Redwood will update retention policy in our system and document in Exhibit A).
- Capacity uplift: one-time line item for a 72-hour burst at 10k tpm. Pricing and billing terms are summarized in the attached PDF.
- Timeline: please review and return redlines by Oct 20. If agreed, we'll route via DocuSign (link below) for signature; once signed we will schedule the evidence staging window for Oct 26–28.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/req/abc123-amendment
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/ACME-42
Drive (evidence plan): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz/SOC2-evidence

If you prefer, we can split the amendment into (A) retention term and (B) one-time capacity addendum so procurement can process the line item independently.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
